newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Nov 22.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- A member of the Selection Committee estimated committee members themselves would occupy about 80 percent of the seats on the provisional legislature.
-- Research by Hong Kong University showed the popularity of Hong Kong Chief Executive candidate Yang Ti Liang was higher than that of Tung Chee-hwa or Peter Woo.

-- MING PAO DAILY -- A senior Chinese official in charge of Taiwan affairs said China had no intention to start talks with Taiwan authorities in the next six months because Taiwan President Li Teng-hui had not abandoned his "two Chinas" stance.
-- Republished books about communist revolutionary heros and heroines have dominated the best-seller list on mainland China.
-- WEN WEI PO -- Coming back from a visit to the United States, the mayor of Shanghai, Xu Kuangdi, brought back a message from U.S. President Bill Clinton that he wanted to visit China next year.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- China Aerospace said it was negotiating with a Malaysian manufacturer over cooperation on automobile production.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China Vest, the long-term investment capital group, was to package two of its best-known investments into a single entity to be floated on the Nasdaq market in the United States.
-- China's reform of its medical reimbursement system, intended to extend coverage to rural areas, will unleash opportunities for foreign pharmaceutical firms.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- There were claims that Beijing was urging trusted Preparatory Committee members to stand for seats on the provisinnal legislature.
